messages.subject: Error using  lkj_corr_cholesky prior
parts:
Hi,


I am pretty new to Stan (and Bayesian modeling in general), and am exploring some of the models described in your really helpful manual. I have been trying to fit a seemingly unrelated regression model like you describe on page 78. With my data, I have noticed that the model becomes increasingly problematic (lots of divergent transitions), as the number of outcomes K increases. In my attempts to get a handle on this, I noticed something with the lkj_corr_cholesky prior that I don't understand. Suppose I have a model as follows:


lkjTest = "


  data {

    int<lower=1> K;               

  }

  parameters {

    cholesky_factor_corr[K] L_Omega;

  }

  model {

    L_Omega ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(2);

  }

  generated quantities {

    corr_matrix[K] corr;

    corr <- multiply_lower_tri_self_transpose(L_Omega);

  }


"


This generally works fine. If K is 30 or larger, however, Stan starts to throw this error: 


 [1] "Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : "                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    

 [2] "  model2107116f846c_fc55120bf3759a2d9575c7b8f269b9c5_namespace::write_array: y is not positive definite:"  


I can make the error go away by replacing corr_matrix[K] with matrix[K,K]. Does this mean that the correlation matrix generated by multiply_lower_tri_self_transpose(L_Omega) is not a valid correlation matrix? If so, is this something I should be concerned about?


Thanks for any help answering my naive questions and for making such a great piece of software.


-Tyler

messages.subject: Re: Error using  lkj_corr_cholesky prior
parts:
On Saturday, February 6, 2016 at 2:35:09 PM UTC-5, Tyler Blazey wrote:
This generally works fine. If K is 30 or larger, however, Stan starts to throw this error: 


 [1] "Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : "                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    

 [2] "  model2107116f846c_fc55120bf3759a2d9575c7b8f269b9c5_namespace::write_array: y is not positive definite:"  


I can make the error go away by replacing corr_matrix[K] with matrix[K,K]. Does this mean that the correlation matrix generated by multiply_lower_tri_self_transpose(L_Omega) is not a valid correlation matrix? If so, is this something I should be concerned about?

You shouldn't be concerned about it, except insofar as it is really difficult to get a large correlation matrix to be numerically positive definite. If L_Omega is a cholesky_factor_corr then multiply_lower_tri_self_transpose(L_Omega) is positive definite by construction, even if it fails is subsequent positive definiteness check, which is why you should not bother to check it, which is why you should declare it as a matrix[K,K] rather than a corr_matrix[K]. Also, this is why you should parameterize your model in terms of Cholesky factors rather than covariance or correlation matrices if at all possible.

Ben
